USER_CONTEXT: Fix Django bug related to `RelatedIn.get_prep_lookup` and `has_select_fields` interaction when `alias()` is used (issue django-16032). Contract requires editing both `django/db/models/fields/related_lookups.py` and `django/db/models/sql/query.py`.

COMPLETED:
- Explored `RelatedIn` class in `django/db/models/fields/related_lookups.py` (lines 75-149): `get_prep_lookup` (76-109), `as_sql` (111-149)
- Explored `Query` methods in `django/db/models/sql/query.py`: `has_select_fields` (267-270), `add_annotation` (1109-1119), `clear_select_fields` (2100-2107), `set_values` (2383-2432), `set_annotation_mask` (2360+), `annotation_select` (2435+)
- Identified root cause: `alias()` calls `add_annotation(select=False)` which converts `annotation_select_mask` from `None` to an explicit set, making `has_select_fields` return True, so `RelatedIn.get_prep_lookup` skips `clear_select_clause()`
- Applied edits to `query.py`: modified `has_select_fields` property and `set_annotation_mask` (reset to `None` when mask covers all annotations)
- Fixed accidental duplication of the `has_select_fields` property
